specGaps: SG-1 — THE JOURNAL/RUN-DIR ORDERING. createJournal(runDir, ...) needs a run directory; the run directory is created by store.createRun(), which needs a store; openWorkspace() needs a journal. That is a genuine cycle and the plan never addresses it. RESOLUTION: a two-phase journal. The plugin constructs ONE journal object whose sink is REBINDABLE: before any run exists it writes through the §7.1 stderr sink (which is what the current stub does, and what plan §3.8/§7.1 specify for pre-run and init-failure output), and the moment a run directory exists it rebinds to the createJournal-backed JSONL sink for that run dir. Records written before the rebind are NOT replayed into the file — they were correctly stderr-only events. CONSIDERED AND REJECTED: (a) buffering pre-run records and flushing them on rebind, which would write records into a run they did not belong to and would break replay's source-order guarantee (Task 15.0 row 15.0-order-file-not-seq); (b) deferring openWorkspace until the first chat.message, which would leave tool.execute.before with no store and is the wrong direction — the gate hook must be able to deny BEFORE any prompt arrives.

SG-2 — NO CONFIG EXISTS ON A FIRST RUN, and Task 12.2 (the writer of .conductor/config.json) has not been built. RESOLUTION: config-io returns {config, repoConfigured}. Absent file ⇒ repoConfigured:false and a documented default Config that is SAFE-BY-CONSTRUCTION rather than permissive: git.mode 'commit' is NOT assumed. This is the first default Config in the product, so it becomes the single source Task 12.2's setup flow must also honour — recorded as a CROSS-TASK OBLIGATION exactly like 12.1's DEFAULT_MAX_READERS, and for the same reason (two independently-authored defaults that drift are invisible to both tasks' tests).

SG-3 — WHICH DIRECTORY IS THE WORKSPACE ROOT. Task 0.2's wire contract established a pinned DRIFT: 'realpath every dir handed to opencode' (conductor/adapter/wire-notes.md). PluginInput carries both `project` and `directory`; conductor/tests/gate-wiring.test.ts:313-333 constructs the factory against `directory: "/repo"`, a path that DOES NOT EXIST. RESOLUTION: the root is the realpath'd `directory`, and openWorkspace is called LAZILY on first use rather than eagerly at factory time — an eager call breaks that committed test, and a plugin that throws at construction ungates the whole session silently (the §3.8 beacon case). A construction-time failure must be loud on stderr and must leave the gate DENYING, never absent.

SG-4 — SCOPE FENCE. This task-let must NOT bind the 22 tool handlers. That is plan:2958's 'glue fixes' and belongs to Task 13.1 (C-044). A row below asserts the fence explicitly, so a future reader can see the boundary was drawn deliberately rather than forgotten.

assertions.text: config-io reads <root>/.conductor/config.json, validates it through the committed validate('Config', parsed) rather than a hand-rolled field check, and returns {config, repoConfigured: true} with the parsed §2.1 values preserved field for field.

an ABSENT config file yields {config: <the documented default>, repoConfigured: false} and does NOT throw — a repo conductor has never been set up in is the ordinary first-run case (§3.2), not an error.

a config file that exists but is unparseable JSON, or parses but fails validate('Config', ...), is a LOUD failure naming the file and the validator's own error text — it must NOT silently fall back to defaults, because a repo whose config says git.mode 'none' silently becoming 'commit' is a security-relevant downgrade.

SG-2: the default Config used when none exists is safe-by-construction — it is asserted field by field against the documented default, and specifically does NOT assume git.mode 'commit'. The same default object is exported as the single source Task 12.2 must honour.

the plugin factory's returned hooks object gains a `chat.message` key of typeof 'function', ALONGSIDE the unchanged `tool` map and the unchanged `tool.execute.before` — both of which are asserted still present and still behaving, so the wiring is additive and cannot have displaced the committed gate hook.

driving the real `chat.message` hook against a real fixture git repo creates a REAL run: run.json exists on disk under the workspace's run directory, is a schema-valid §2.3 Run, and carries the prompt text and the provisional classification handleChatMessage supplies. Asserted by reading the file, not by trusting the hook's return value.

after that same hook call the arriving sessionID is registered with role 'orchestrator' in the registry the PLUGIN holds — asserted through the registry the gate hook actually consults, not a test-local copy. This is the row whose absence made Task 10.1 unimplementable against the product.

the load-bearing end-to-end row: an edit from a session that has NOT sent a chat.message is denied as unregistered, and the SAME edit from the SAME session AFTER a chat.message is adjudicated as the orchestrator. One registry, two consumers, proven by behaviour change rather than by inspecting a Map.

a second chat.message arriving while the first run is live is routed into it — no second run directory is created, the run count on disk stays 1, and the hook's result names the LIVE runId (chat-message.ts:118-122's routed-midrun path, reached through the plugin rather than called directly).

SG-1: records written BEFORE any run exists go to the stderr sink and create no file; the moment a run directory exists the journal rebinds and subsequent records land in <runDir>/journal.jsonl as schema-valid JournalRecords. Asserted by reading the file and by capturing the stderr sink — including the negative half, that pre-run records are NOT replayed into the file.

SG-3: the factory does NOT open the workspace at construction (the committed gate-wiring test constructs it against a non-existent directory and must keep passing), and when it does open, the root is the REALPATH of input.directory — asserted through a symlinked fixture root, since the §0.2 wire contract pins realpath as a DRIFT and a symlinked root is exactly how the scope gates would silently mis-match.

if the workspace cannot be opened (unreadable root, foreign live lock), the failure is written to the §7.1 stderr sink naming the cause AND the gate hook still DENIES rather than being absent — a plugin that fails open is the §3.8 silent-ungate case, which the wire contract records as the most dangerous failure shape in the integration.

a throw from inside handleChatMessage (injected via a store whose createRun throws) is CAUGHT by the hook, journaled once at error level, and does NOT propagate out of the hook — G5 fail-soft: conductor failing must not take the user's opencode session down with it.

SG-4, the deliberate NEGATIVE row: every one of the 22 CONDUCTOR_TOOL_NAMES is still bound to a handler that throws the handlerNotBound message. This task-let takes the lifecycle half of the composition root and NOT the tool-to-handler binding, which is plan:2958's glue and Task 13.1's. Asserting the fence makes the boundary visible instead of leaving a future reader to wonder whether it was forgotten.

The gate hook's git policy is READ FROM THE LOADED CONFIG, not hardcoded. plugin/index.ts:508-510 now passes `gitMode: config.git.mode` and `branchPolicy: config.git.branchPolicy` into gateBeforeToolCall, replacing the committed hardcoded "commit"/"pin". Asserted by BEHAVIOUR CHANGE through the real plugin hook, both directions: with `.conductor/config.json` carrying git.mode "read-only", a registered session's `bash` call `git commit -m x` is denied with the READ-ONLY reason; with the same call under git.mode "commit" it is denied with the DIFFERENT (conductor_publish) reason. The negative control matters as much as the positive - a test that only checks 'denied' passes against a hardcoded policy, since both configurations deny.
